title: Traditional Indian Ghati Clock
intro: This clock counts traditional Indian ghati and pala units from the most recent calculated sunrise.
structure: One ghati equals 24 ordinary minutes, or 60 pala. One pala equals 24 ordinary seconds. A nominal 24-hour day contains 60 ghati. Both displayed counts start at zero; the pala field cycles from 0 to 59.
example: At sunrise the reading is 0 ghati, 0 pala. One ordinary hour later it is 2 ghati, 30 pala; after 24 minutes it is 1 ghati, 0 pala.
history: Ghati and pala are traditional Indian time divisions. Sunrise-based reckoning is represented here as a modern computational model, not a claim to replicate all historical clocks or calendrical schools.
model: Compute sunrise from compact solar equation-of-time and declination terms, the supplied coordinates and a 0.833-degree horizon correction. Select the latest valid event in a bounded search. Floor the elapsed ordinary seconds, divide by 1440 for ghati and use floor(elapsed/24) modulo 60 for pala. Search for the next visible change at millisecond resolution.
limits: The nominal day has fixed-size units, but the elapsed count is not artificially clamped to 59 ghati before the next sunrise. Invalid coordinates fail, and an undefined solar origin produces N/A. The seconds toggle does not add subdivisions. The computation does not establish historical observational accuracy. The solar model assumes an idealised sea-level horizon and standard depression; local terrain and weather are not modelled.
